comments.content: This call site violates the invariant that `normalizeInstalledTag` (and `UpdateVerdict.Result.codesAlreadyMatch` / `adoptMatchedTag`'s "sole legitimate installed-tag rewrite") rely on: rewriting `installedVersion` to the latest tag is only legitimate when the installed APK's versionCode already equals the *latest* build's. The guard above (`systemInfo.versionCode != existing.installedVersionCode`) only proves the DB row is in sync with the system, not that the running binary is the latest release. Concretely: installed code 140 / tag "1.4.0", `latestVersion` = "v1.5.0" / `latestVersionCode` = 150, DB in sync → every app start rewrites the tag to "v1.5.0" and forces `isUpdateAvailable = false`. From then on `UpdateVerdict.decide` sees `installed.tag == matched.tag` (`isVersionNewer(x, x)` = false, `codesAlreadyMatch` = false since 140 ≠ 150), so the real self-update is never re-offered and the UI claims a version the user isn't running. Behavior is inherited from the previous inline `copy()`, but this PR is precisely about reliably detecting updates, and this is the only call site of `normalizeInstalledTag` that doesn't establish its precondition. Fix: bail when the installed code doesn't match the latest snapshot (fold it into the guard above so the misleading "Normalized ..." log is skipped too).

**Finding 1 (high, bug):** `normalizeSelfInstalledVersion` call to `existing.normalizeInstalledTag(latestTag)` at line ~271. Precondition violation: the guard checks `systemInfo.versionCode != existing.installedVersionCode` (DB↔system consistency) but the project invariant (per `UpdateVerdict.Result.codesAlreadyMatch` and `adoptMatchedTag`'s "sole legitimate installed-tag rewrite" comment) requires the installed code to equal the *latest build's* code before rewriting the installed tag and clearing `isUpdateAvailable`. With a genuine pending self-update (installed code 140/tag "1.4.0", latest "v1.5.0"/code 150) and DB in sync with the system, this startup path rewrites `installedVersion` to "v1.5.0" and forces `isUpdateAvailable=false`. Future `UpdateVerdict.decide` runs see `installed.tag == matched.tag` so `isVersionNewer(x,x)=false`, `codesAlreadyMatch=false` (140≠150), `usedTimestampLogic=false` → the update is never re-offered: the self-update is permanently hidden and the UI mislabels the installed version. Fix: bail unless `existing.latestVersionCode == systemInfo.versionCode`:

```kotlin
if (systemInfo.versionCode != existing.installedVersionCode) return
// rewriting the installed tag is only legitimate when the package really is
// the latest build (cf. UpdateVerdict.codesAlreadyMatch)
if (existing.latestVersionCode != systemInfo.versionCode) return
repo.updateApp(existing.normalizeInstalledTag(latestTag))
```

Trace for a tracked semver app (tag v1.0.0, code 10) whose user side-loads v2.0.0 (code 20): resolveExternalInstallVerdict() correctly says UP_TO_DATE (20 >= 10) and writes isUpdateAvailable=false, but the follow-up checkForUpdates() computes UpdateVerdict with Installed(tag="v1.0.0" stale, code=20) vs Matched(tag="v2.0.0") — codesAlreadyMatch is false (20 != 10), usedTimestampLogic is false, so it falls through to isVersionNewer("v2.0.0", "v1.0.0") = true and overwrites the flag. It never self-heals: updateVersionInfo(latestVersionCode = resolvedLatestVersionCode) writes NULL when the matched tag differs from the stored latest tag, so adoptMatchedTag's codesAlreadyMatch gate (requires latestVersionCode > 0) can never fire again — the badge and the stale tag persist until the user pointlessly reinstalls the same build. (Writing systemInfo.versionName into the tag column, as before, accidentally kept isVersionNewer() false here — that is the behaviour being regressed.) Fix: don't let the stale tag drive the flag — after checkForUpdates() refreshes the snapshot, re-apply resolveExternalInstallVerdict() against the refreshed row (or pass systemInfo.versionCode into checkForUpdates() so UpdateVerdict can treat an installed code ahead of the stored snapshot as caught-up and adopt the matched tag).

The comment justifies hash tails with "the same name legitimately comes back as a different build", but a hash tail IS build identity — that is why versionsReconcilable refuses to compare these tags and why the tests treat `26.08.11f15e4` as naming exactly one build. comments.content: False-positive regression for versions with a single-letter build/alpha suffix: `1.2.3b1234`, `2.0.5a2024`, `2026.09.23a1` all match (the tail `3b1234` / `23a1` is 4+ chars of [0-9a-f] and contains one a-f letter), so they are now preserved verbatim and classified as hash tails. Before this PR normalizeVersion truncated them via DOTTED_DIGIT_PATTERN to `1.2.3` / `2026.09.23` and compared numerically. Now versionsReconcilable returns false, and for a release that is not GitHub-flagged prerelease and has no marker word, UpdateVerdict falls to `!reconcilable -> false` — the update is silently never reported. Tighten the tail to require at least two hex letters (a real hash tail like `11f15e4`/`fabc` has ≥2; `3b1234` has 1), or explicitly exclude the `digits + single letter + digits` build-suffix shape. The pinned tests (`26.08.11f15e4`, `26.08.ac0a687`, `1.2.3fabc`) all keep ≥2 letters and still pass.

comments.content: This matcher is `VersionMath.isSameVersion`, a normalized *numeric* comparison, and `normalizeVersion` collapses marker-prefixed tags to their bare number (`"beta-6" -> "6"`, `"rc1" -> "1"`, `"m5" -> "5"` — the same collapse the display label already suffers from). Consequently `isSameVersion("rc1", "v1") == true`: in a repo with tags `v1` (stable) and `rc1` (pre), the newest-first `firstOrNull` can match the wrong release and flip the initial channel in either direction — a stable `v1` user is pushed onto PRE_RELEASE and a `rc1` user onto STABLE, i.e. the exact misdirection this PR aims to fix. The tag identity used by the update check (`UpdateVerdict.sameTag`) and by `SmartInstallButton` in this same feature is `isExactSameVersion` (which already strips `v`/`refs/tags/`/word prefixes, so it still matches the versionName-style `installedVersion` written by import/self-registration). Prefer an exact tag match first and keep `isSameVersion` only as a fallback for spelling variants like `2.1.0` vs `2.1.0-full`. Capturing the matched release in a val also fixes the discarded-match problem noted above (the matched release is the channel the user is actually on).

comments.content: `isUpdateAvailable = false` is hard-coded on code-match, which re-introduces the reused-tag bug class this PR fixes. For a re-published nightly the same versionCode can carry a newer build, so the stored flag may be a legitimate timestamp-based `true` verdict — the exact state `adoptMatchedTag` (InstalledAppsRepositoryImpl) explicitly guards by forwarding the verdict instead of hard-coding `false` ("Hard-coding false here would wipe that correct 'update available' result"). Worse, clearing the flag also defeats `VersionMath.shouldReportTimestampUpdate`, which re-reports a superseded release via `previousWasUpdateAvailable && isExactSameVersion(...)` — once wiped, the update stays hidden until the next publish. Make the caller's computed verdict a parameter (like adoptMatchedTag) instead of assuming false.

comments.content: Both call sites of `recordTransientFailure` (this empty-window site and the `resolved == null` miss below) funnel deterministic, often *persistent* states into a policy written for transient fetch failures: with `fallbackToOlderReleases = false` a newer release that fails the asset filter shadows the tracked one forever (`resolveTrackedRelease` only inspects `take(1)`), a pinned variant/asset name can be renamed away, or the repo can go pre-release-only while `includePreReleases = false`. In those states the `isTimestampTrackedTag` branch only bumps `lastCheckedAt`, freezing a previously earned `isUpdateAvailable = true` badge forever — the old `clearUpdateMetadata` self-healed it — even though, per the user's own filter semantics, the update target is expired, while `lastCheckedAt` keeps looking healthy. The preserve-branch is only correct when the fetch *failed* (the release presumably still exists and re-reporting from a null baseline is the risk). Fix: distinguish "fetch failed" from "fetch succeeded but nothing matched" — e.g. have `fetchReleaseWindow`/`fetchForgejoReleaseWindow` return `null` on failure vs `emptyList()` on genuine emptiness — and on a successful no-match clear `isUpdateAvailable` while *keeping* `latestReleasePublishedAt` (needs a narrow column-level DAO update; `clearUpdateMetadata` wipes the baseline this PR is protecting).

This confirm path silently destroys the exact state the nightly-reuse fix depends on. `confirmInstall` recomputes `isUpdateAvailable` via `isVersionNewer(latestVersion, tag)` and reconciles `latestVersionCode` to the installed code whenever that is false. For a reused tag both sides are e.g. `nightly`, so `isVersionNewer("nightly", "nightly")` is *always* false — the timestamp-derived badge is unconditionally wiped and `latestVersionCode` is stamped with the confirmed build's code.

Trace (the PR's headline scenario): `nightly` build A(code 100) installed; maintainer re-publishes the tag as build B(105)@T2 → `checkForUpdates` raises the badge via `usedTimestampLogic` and stores `latestReleasePublishedAt=T2` (keeping `latestVersionCode=100`, since `matchedRelease.tagName == app.latestVersion`). Now a PACKAGE_REPLACED lands while/after the user confirms an install of a build older or different than the T2 build (e.g. `versionCodeMatchesTarget` passes against the stale expected code 100 when build 100 is reinstalled; or a newer T3 publish happened while B was parked and the user installs B). `updateAppVersion` → `confirmInstall` clears `isUpdateAvailable`. On the next check, `shouldReportTimestampUpdate` finds `matchedPublishedAt == stored.publishedAt` (T2/T3 already baselined) and its only re-arm — `previousWasUpdateAvailable && isExactSameVersion(...)` — is now dead, so the verdict is `false` forever. The update is never offered again until a new publish. This is reachable from both call sites of `updateAppVersion` (`PackageEventReceiver` pending-confirm and `InstallationManagerImpl`'s normal install flow).

Pre-PR this state couldn't exist (reused tags never raised a badge), so the fix introduces a new invariant that this write breaks. Durable fix: record the downloaded artifact's publish point (e.g. park `latestReleasePublishedAt` alongside `pendingInstallVersion/AssetName`) and have the confirm logic clear the timestamp-derived flag only when the artifact's publish point matches the stored `latestReleasePublishedAt`; if it is older, keep the badge. At minimum, for `VersionMath.isTimestampTrackedTag(tag)` builds, `confirmInstall` must not overwrite `isUpdateAvailable`/`latestVersionCode` on the `isVersionNewer(tag, tag) == false` branch.
